text:
sam.infra: Heads-up — since the privkey rotation landed (~10m ago) APAC GPU nodes are failing nodejoin. Looks like our firewall strict-mode + new KMS grant TTL caused the audit-shipper to drop auth requests. Seeing ~40% fewer GPUs in the pool.

julia-sre: @sam.infra can you paste the join error? is it a 403 from the KMS proxy or connection reset from the audit endpoint? :eyes:

sam.infra: Error snippet from node logs: `2026-03-23T10:14:02Z ERROR nodejoin auth failed: kms:DecryptDenied; audit-shipper: connection refused`

maria-sec: We rotated the ephemeral privkeys per policy. The KMS grant TTL was shortened in the same rollout — curious the canary didn't catch the audit-shipper backpressure. I'm going to check grant propagation.

deployment-bot: Canary job #apac-priv-rot-3: 5/8 nodes failed join within 120s. Rolling status -> paused.

ops-bot: Alert: apac-gpu-pool size down 38% (expected 6 -> 4), autoscaler triggered burst capacity (spot fallback). Cost projection +18% for next 24h.

julia-sre: Temporary mitigation options: 1) revert KMS TTL change 2) add audit-shipper VPC allows for the new privkey signer IP range 3) relax firewall strict-mode to allow existing grants to finish. Which is least blasty?

maria-sec: Reverting TTL is safe but needs a key policy change — will require minor IAM window. Adding VPC allowlist for signer IPs is fastest (no cross-account key edits). I can open an allowlist exception for 1 hour.

chris-ml: Impact: TB-dev and embedding-training jobs got preempted; reschedules will flood the cluster when nodes come back. Heads up for possible queue pressure.

sam.infra: Let's do the allowlist first. @maria-sec can you open the ephemeral allow for `10.88.12.0/24`? If that stabilizes we can plan a TTL revert in maintenance window.

maria-sec: Opening allowlist now. Patch command (internal):
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-xyz --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.88.12.0/24
```

maria-sec: Done. Audit-shipper connections recovering. Monitoring.

deployment-bot: Canary re-run: 8/8 nodes joined within 90s. Status -> healthy.

ops-bot: Pool size back to expected. Cost projection corrected. :thumbsup:

julia-sre: Follow-ups: - run a targeted eval to ensure no silent auth regressions - schedule an off-peak TTL revert test with canary route - add the privkey signer IPs to our canary acceptance tests

sam.infra: Agree. I'll open a follow-up ticket and schedule the TTL revert for Tuesday 0300 UTC. Also adding a short runbook snippet to the incident notes: `If privkey rotation + firewall strict-mode coincides, allowlist signer CIDR or revert TTL`

maria-sec: We'll also add an automated smoke test: after any key rotation, exercise audit-shipper endpoints from signer subnets.

chris-ml: Thanks y'all — I'll ramp the job reschedules slowly to avoid a sudden spike.

sam.infra: Closing this thread — marking as resolved for now. Ping me if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:
